title: Finite Tor dimension forces injectivity on ideal generator spaces
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $K\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be ideals. Suppose that $A/J$, as an $A/K$-module through the quotient map, has finite Tor dimension: there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $\operatorname{Tor}^{A/K}_i(A/J,N)=0$ for every $A/K$-module $N$ and every integer $i>d$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Then the natural $A/\mathfrak m$-linear map $K/\mathfrak mK\longrightarrow J/\mathfrak mJ$, $x\bmod\mathfrak mK\longmapsto x\bmod\mathfrak mJ$, is injective. Here $\mathfrak mK$ and $\mathfrak mJ$ are product ideals, viewed as submodules of $K$ and $J$, respectively. The ideals may be zero or equal.

source.place: Tag 09PV (lemma-injective); finite Tor dimension expanded as an ordinary module Tor bound.

proof.text: The map is well defined since $\mathfrak mK\subseteq\mathfrak mJ$. If its kernel is nonzero, choose $f\in K\cap\mathfrak mJ$ with $f\notin\mathfrak mK$. Set $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Noetherianity makes $K/\mathfrak mK$ finite dimensional. Extend its nonzero vector $\bar f$ to a basis, and let $\lambda:K/\mathfrak mK\to k$ be its first coordinate, so $\lambda(\bar f)=1$. The preimage $K'$ of $\ker\lambda$ in $K$ is an ideal (the action factors through $k$), contains $\mathfrak mK$, and $K/K'$ is generated by the nonzero image of $f$.

Put $R'=A/K'$, $R=A/K$, and $\epsilon=f\bmod K'$. Both quotient rings are Noetherian: lift an ideal to $A$ and project a finite generating set. The kernel of $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ is $(\epsilon)=K/K'$, and its square is zero since $K^2\subseteq\mathfrak mK\subseteq K'$. Its annihilator in $R$ is $I=\mathfrak m/K$: elements of $\mathfrak m$ kill $f\bmod K'$, whereas any $c\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit, so $cf\in K'$ would imply $f\in K'$, a contradiction.

Choose finite ideal generators $a_1,\ldots,a_t$ of $J$, using Noetherianity. As $f\in\mathfrak mJ$, expanding in these generators gives $f=\sum_jb_ja_j$ with $b_j\in\mathfrak m$. In the obstruction node take zero polynomial variables, $h_j=a_j\bmod K$, $r_j=b_j\bmod K$, and the lifts $h'_j=a_j\bmod K'$, $r'_j=b_j\bmod K'$. Then $\sum_jr_jh_j=0$, all $r_j\in I$, and $\sum_jr'_jh'_j=\epsilon=1\epsilon$. Here $S=R/(h_j)=A/J$, and $S/IS=A/\mathfrak m=k\ne0$ because $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Thus the coefficient $g'=1$ has nonnilpotent image.

Apply the square-zero relation obstruction with the data just verified. It says that $S=A/J$ admits no bound on $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_i(S,N)$ valid for every $R$-module $N$. This contradicts the given finite Tor dimension over $R=A/K$. Therefore the kernel vector chosen in step 1 cannot exist, and the asserted map is injective.

Step 1 (elementary): K/mK is finite-dimensional because K is finitely generated; the coordinate λ with λ(f̄)=1 gives an ideal K', since A acts on K/mK through k; K/K' is generated by f. Step 2 (elementary): square zero holds because K²⊆mK⊆K'. The annihilator is exactly m/K: m kills f, and a unit c with cf∈K' would force f∈K'; it is well defined because K·f⊆K'. Step 3 (elementary): f∈mJ gives coefficients b_j∈m; Σr_jh_j = f mod K = 0; the lifts give ε, so g'=1; with n=0, S=A/J and S/IS=k≠0. Every hypothesis of the obstruction node is checked. Step 4: the obstruction's conclusion contradicts the Tor bound for the same R-module A/J over A/K. New node lem-sfb-square-zero-relation-tor-obstruction: faithful to 09PU; the explicit lift g' in P' is equivalent to Stacks' g∈(R/I)[x].
